title: Five ways to integrate a SystemSketch Dev Hub
brief: Add one Dev icon beside Help in the existing bottom-right utility strip, then make Stable, Latest Preview, and named isolated presets easy to launch and manage without making the ordinary canvas feel like a development tool.
defaultWhy: Anchored Dev Shelf is the provisional default at 96.8/100. It matches the user's chosen placement, reuses the current Help-popover geometry, keeps the ordinary canvas quiet, and gives Latest Preview plus isolated presets enough room without turning development state into permanent chrome.
decisionHinge: The recommendation assumes launching or browsing a preset is the common task and lifecycle administration is occasional. If Zach begins switching presets many times per hour, V3 Quick Switch becomes more attractive; if he needs build and session state visible while drawing, V2 Dev Drawer should replace the popover.
invariants: A dedicated Dev icon sits immediately before the existing Help icon in the bottom-right utility strip.
Help returns to user help and shortcuts; release status, Latest Preview, publishing, preset launch, and preset lifecycle move into Dev.
Stable is the ordinary immutable entry; Latest Preview and isolated presets reuse the one live Preview runtime.
Every experimental launch opens an independent board copy and labels the active composition after launch.
Dev UI state and preset lifecycle metadata never enter .tldr document content.
boundary: Standalone interactive UI prototypes in one common SystemSketch canvas frame. Opening, switching, archive views, stories, and selection controls work inside the gallery; no Dev icon, preset registry, launcher endpoint, clone transaction, or production SystemSketch behavior has been implemented.

requirements.name: Fast focused switching
requirements.why: The Dev destination should help Zach enter one isolated working context without reconstructing configuration or scanning unrelated controls.
requirements.passCondition: From the normal canvas, Block Dev or Latest Preview can be identified and launched in at most two obvious actions.

anchors.1: Requires several screens or configuration choices.
anchors.3: Reachable in two or three actions but demands interpretation.
anchors.5: The intended target is immediately legible and launches in one or two obvious actions.

requirements.name: Ordinary canvas stays calm
requirements.why: Development affordances are valuable only when they do not make Stable or normal drawing feel like an engineering console.
requirements.passCondition: At rest, the only added chrome is one quiet Dev icon beside Help; detail appears only on request.

anchors.1: Persistent labels, badges, or panels dominate normal drawing.
anchors.3: Mostly quiet, with some ongoing development state visible.
anchors.5: One quiet icon at rest; all detail is progressive disclosure.

requirements.name: State and safety are unmistakable
requirements.why: Stable, Latest Preview, and isolated compositions must not blur together or threaten the working document.
requirements.passCondition: Before launch, the surface names channel, composition, and independent-copy policy; after launch, the active composition is visibly identified.

anchors.1: Targets look interchangeable or document ownership is hidden.
anchors.3: Safety exists but appears only in secondary detail.
anchors.5: Channel, composition, and copy policy are clear at decision time and after launch.

requirements.name: Lifecycle remains manageable
requirements.why: The selector should not become an attic as experiments accumulate and are replaced.
requirements.passCondition: Active presets stay clean while archived presets, successor links, and management actions remain discoverable.

anchors.1: No visible retirement path or archived history.
anchors.3: Management exists but is distant from the launch surface.
anchors.5: Active and archived states are easy to understand and manage without clutter.

requirements.name: Fits the current utility seam
requirements.why: SystemSketch already has a tldraw toolbar, anchored Help panel, right popout, focus handling, and mutually exclusive bottom-right surfaces.
requirements.passCondition: The concept can reuse those components and interaction conventions without replacing the toolbar or introducing a second global navigation system.

anchors.1: Requires a new shell or conflicts with existing canvas chrome.
anchors.3: Reuses some primitives but adds significant navigation machinery.
anchors.5: Extends the existing toolbar/popover model with a sibling trigger and shared state.

hardGates.name: Dev is distinct from Help
hardGates.why: Developer operations should no longer hide inside end-user help once a dedicated destination exists.

hardGates.name: Stable and document safety remain explicit
hardGates.why: No launcher treatment may weaken the immutable Stable anchor or independent-copy rule.

hardGates.name: No document mutation from UI selection
hardGates.why: Choosing, pinning, or archiving a development context is application metadata, never board content.

variants.name: Anchored Dev Shelf
variants.thesis: Mirror the current Help popover with a sibling Dev panel: Latest Preview first, isolated presets second, management last.
variants.bestWhen: Most visits are deliberate launches into a known context and development details should disappear completely afterward.
variants.losesWhen: You need persistent build diagnostics or switch contexts dozens of times without closing the surface.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.value: A </> icon immediately before Help; clicking it closes Help and any right popout.

decisions.label: Hierarchy
decisions.value: Latest Preview is the primary row, named isolated presets form a compact shelf, and Archived/Manage stays in the footer.

decisions.label: After launch
decisions.value: The existing top-center Preview badge gains the active preset name, for example Preview · Block Dev.

keepParts: Latest Preview as the primary row
active shelf with quiet archive footer
proof: The common canvas shows only one additional </> icon at rest and a product-matched 370px panel when opened.
The direct Archive action removes Block Dev from Active and exposes an archived successor row without changing the canvas.

fr1.evidence: Latest Preview and Block Dev are visible immediately after one icon click; each row is a single launch target.

fr2.evidence: At rest the existing strip gains only one icon; the anchored panel is transient and mutually exclusive with Help.

fr3.evidence: Every row names Live tree, its composition, and independent copy; Stable is fixed at the top of the panel.

fr4.evidence: Archive is understandable and the footer exposes history, though bulk administration belongs in a secondary manager.

fr5.evidence: It is structurally the existing Help panel plus a sibling trigger and shared open-surface state.

g1.evidence: Help and Dev remain separate adjacent triggers with mutually exclusive panels.

g2.evidence: Stable is labeled immutable and every development row says independent copy.

g3.evidence: Archive and launch state live entirely in the panel prototype.

variants.name: Persistent Dev Drawer
variants.thesis: Treat Dev as a real right-side workspace that can stay open while you inspect builds, presets, sessions, and archives on the canvas.
variants.bestWhen: Development status and preset management are part of the work itself, not just a launch transition.
variants.losesWhen: You want the drawing surface to feel completely ordinary between occasional preview launches.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.value: The </> icon toggles a full-height inset right popout through the existing right-surface provider.

decisions.label: Hierarchy
decisions.value: A compact navigation rail switches between Launch, Running, and Archived without closing the canvas.

decisions.label: After launch
decisions.value: The drawer remains available as an environment inspector until explicitly closed.

proof: The prototype keeps Robot sorter visible while a product-matched inset drawer exposes complete development context.
The direct tab action switches from launch targets to archived presets and successor metadata in place.

fr1.evidence: Launch targets are direct, though entering the drawer and its navigation adds more visual scanning than V1.

fr2.evidence: The drawer is absent at rest but designed to remain open, taking a meaningful slice of canvas during development.

fr3.evidence: Persistent channel, build, document, and active-composition facts are the drawer's strongest feature.

fr4.evidence: Running and Archived are first-class destinations with room for successor and retention metadata.

fr5.evidence: It can reuse the existing rightSurface provider, but competes with board overview and inspector popouts.

g1.evidence: The Dev icon opens a dedicated drawer; Help stays an adjacent separate trigger.

g2.evidence: A persistent safety card labels Stable and independent-copy launch policy.

g3.evidence: Tabs and lifecycle controls are application UI state only.

variants.name: Quick Switch Menu
variants.thesis: Optimize the Dev icon for the next launch: Latest Preview and recent presets first, with configuration pushed behind Manage.
variants.bestWhen: You repeatedly bounce among two or three known contexts and almost never edit preset definitions from the launcher.
variants.losesWhen: You need to understand composition ingredients, build details, or retirement history before choosing.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.value: A very small menu opens directly above the </> icon and remembers the most recently used targets.

decisions.label: Hierarchy
decisions.value: Latest Preview is the default action; recent isolated presets follow; Manage is deliberately secondary.

decisions.label: After launch
decisions.value: A short confirmation state names the opened preset and independent copy, then the menu dismisses.

proof: The menu fits within the current strip's visual scale and exposes the three likely launches with minimal text.
The direct Open action changes to a clear Block Dev launch confirmation using the same state as the guided story.

fr1.evidence: One icon click and one row click launch the latest or recent isolated context with almost no scanning.

fr2.evidence: The transient menu is the smallest proposed surface and adds only one icon at rest.

fr3.evidence: Rows say copy and the confirmation is explicit, but composition/build detail is intentionally compressed.

fr4.evidence: Lifecycle work is delegated to Manage; archived history is not visible in the primary menu.

fr5.evidence: It easily fits the toolbar, though it introduces a second lighter menu style alongside the fuller Help panel.

g1.evidence: The quick menu belongs only to the Dev icon; Help is unaffected.

g2.evidence: Every development target includes the copy glyph and the confirmation states Stable stayed open.

g3.evidence: Recent ordering and confirmation are launcher state.

steps.label: Choose from recent targets
steps.caption: The surface assumes you already know Block Dev and Rows Lab, so it optimizes for recognition and speed.

steps.label: Confirm the safe launch
steps.caption: A brief confirmation names Block Dev, its composition, and the independent board copy before dismissing.

media.label: Focus loop
media.caption: This direction aggressively optimizes the common transition and delegates administration.

variants.name: Dev Command Palette
variants.thesis: Make the Dev icon open a centered, keyboard-first command surface that searches presets, build actions, and lifecycle operations together.
variants.bestWhen: The preset catalog grows large or agents and keyboard users need one reproducible command vocabulary.
variants.losesWhen: The catalog stays small and you want the available development contexts to teach themselves visually.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.value: The </> icon invokes a centered command palette; Cmd+Shift+D opens the same surface.

decisions.label: Hierarchy
decisions.value: Search spans Open, Manage, Archive, Publish, and Return actions rather than presenting a fixed shelf.

decisions.label: After launch
decisions.value: The selected result expands to show channel, composition, and copy policy before confirmation.

proof: The hero renders a credible command surface over the same SystemSketch canvas with grouped realistic results.
The direct Select action expands Block Dev into a safety-confirmation state driven by the guided story.

fr1.evidence: Known targets are very fast by keyboard, but browsing requires search/result interpretation instead of recognition from a shelf.

fr2.evidence: Only the Dev icon persists; the modal command surface is completely transient.

fr3.evidence: The confirmation state is explicit, though the initial result list compresses important safety context.

fr4.evidence: Archive and restore commands are searchable, but lifecycle history is not spatially legible without a query.

fr5.evidence: It can reuse dialogs and typed actions but adds a global command-index layer beyond the current Help popover.

g1.evidence: The palette is explicitly titled Dev commands and invoked from its own icon.

g2.evidence: Opening a result reveals the independent-copy contract before confirmation.

g3.evidence: Commands mutate launcher or manifest state only.

steps.label: Search the command vocabulary
steps.caption: A single query finds presets and related lifecycle actions without a separate settings hierarchy.

steps.label: Inspect before opening
steps.caption: The selected Block Dev command expands to show Live tree, stock + Block, and independent copy before launch.

media.label: Shared protocol
media.caption: The same named commands can later back the UI, keyboard shortcuts, URLs, and agent tooling.

variants.name: Expanding Dev Ribbon
variants.thesis: Let the Dev icon temporarily expand the utility strip itself into a horizontal context switcher for Stable, Latest, and pinned isolated presets.
variants.bestWhen: Context switching is extremely frequent and the current development context should remain one glance away from the canvas.
variants.losesWhen: The bottom-right corner must remain compact or preset lifecycle work matters more than rapid switching.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.value: The same </> icon expands leftward into pinned context chips without opening a separate panel.

decisions.label: Hierarchy
decisions.value: Stable, Latest, Block Dev, and Rows Lab behave like environment tabs; overflow opens full management.

decisions.label: After launch
decisions.value: The active context remains selected in the ribbon until it collapses or the user returns to Stable.

proof: The prototype demonstrates the exact strip expansion against the same bottom toolbar and canvas geometry.
The direct control uses one state machine to expand and collapse pinned development contexts.

fr1.evidence: Pinned contexts become direct one-click targets immediately beside the current canvas controls.

fr2.evidence: The collapsed state is quiet, but the expanded ribbon is wide, visually dense, and can compete with the bottom toolbar.

fr3.evidence: Active context is continuously visible, though compact chips have little room for document-copy explanations.

fr4.evidence: Pinning keeps the ribbon curated and overflow reaches management, but archived history is off-surface.

fr5.evidence: It modifies the geometry and responsive behavior of the existing utility strip rather than adding a sibling popover.

g1.evidence: The expansion originates only from the dedicated Dev icon beside Help.

g2.evidence: Stable is a fixed chip and every development chip carries a copy marker in its tooltip/label.

g3.evidence: Pin and selected-context state remain application metadata.
